module: Physical state of the vehicle on the Lua side (vehicle VM, global `beamstate`). Tracks broken or deformed beams, break groups (breakGroup) and deform groups (deformGroup), the damage score per part and per body zone, flat tires, planets (local gravity attractors) and all couplers (hitches, trailers). A modder uses it to break groups, puncture tires, add damage, read damage, attach or detach couplers, save or load the state of nodes and beams. The hooks beamBroken, onBeamDeformed, onCouplerAttached and onCouplerDetached are called by the C++ engine; updateGFX and init/reset by the vehicle's main loop.
usage:
-- break a group, puncture a tire, read the damage
beamstate.breakBreakGroup("doorFL_break")
beamstate.deflateTire(0)
local zones = beamstate.getBodyZoneDamage() -- {FL=0..1, FR=..., ML, MR, RL, RR}
print(beamstate.damage)
-- toggle couplers
beamstate.toggleCouplers()
notes: `beamstate.damage` = dissipated energy of the engine (`obj:getDissipatedEnergy()`) + `damageExt`, recomputed on every updateGFX. `damageExt` is incremented by addDamage and by 1000 each time a tire deflates.
Beam, node, wheel and triangle ids are `cid` (0-based engine index).
Body zones: letter 1 = front/middle/rear (F, M, R according to y in thirds), letter 2 = L/R according to x (half). Wheel beams (wheelID) do not count. Damage values from 0 to about 1.
breakGroupType of a beam: 0 or nil = breaking this beam breaks the whole group; 1 = the beam is broken by the group but does not trigger it.
A beam with `beamPrecompressionTime` (or a torsion bar with `precompressionTime`) activates `M.update` during the progressive precompression time; afterwards `M.update` goes back to `nop`.

M.update, M.updateRemoteElectrics and M.debugDraw are `nop` (the game's empty function) and not nil; the fields listed as `nop` references are therefore empty functions. `update` is active only during precompression; `updateRemoteElectrics` is installed at the first coupler data export; `debugDraw` is active as long as coupler visibility is requested.

Potential bug: in init, `for _, tag in b.tag do` (and the linkTag variant) iterates without `pairs`, so a beam whose `tag` or `linkTag` is a table causes a Lua error. The linkTag branch also tests `type(b.tag)` instead of `type(b.linkTag)`.
Potential bug: onCouplerAttached reads `n.breakGroup` without checking that `n` (node) is non-nil, whereas the previous test checks it.
`beamstate.getVehicleState` contains a deliberate fake 1-second delay (busy-wait loop) and a warning log: do not call it in a game loop.

`brokenBreakGroups` is replaced by a new table on every init/reset: do not keep an old reference. On the other hand `deformedBeams`, `couplerCache`, `attachedCouplers`, `nodeNameMap`, `tagBeamMap` are emptied then filled in place.
Fields exported but never written in this file: `lowpressure` is set to true as soon as a tire is deflated and reset to false only by reset().

damage.desc: Cumulative vehicle damage (dissipated energy + damageExt), updated in updateGFX.

damageExt.desc: Artificially added damage (addDamage, punctured tires +1000). Reset to 0 by init.

lowpressure.desc: true as soon as at least one tire has been deflated. Reset to false by reset().

brokenBreakGroups.desc: Names of the breakGroups already broken (value true). Table recreated on every init.

deformGroupDamage.desc: Per deformGroup: {eventCount, damage, maxEvents, invMaxEvents}. `damage` = eventCount / maxEvents, from 0 to about 1.

deformGroupsTriggerBeam.desc: Per deformGroup, cid of the first beam that triggered it (deformation or break).

activeParts.desc: Names of the active parts of the vehicle, collected from `v.data.slotMap`.

monetaryDamage.desc: Reset to 0 by init, not modified elsewhere in this file.

nodeNameMap.desc: Jbeam name of a node -> cid.

tagBeamMap.desc: Beam tag -> list of ids of beams carrying this tag.

linkTagBeamMap.desc: Beam linkTag -> list of beam ids.

deformedBeams.desc: Alias of beamDamageTracker: per beam cid, deformation ratio (onBeamDeformed) or 1 if broken.

couplerCache.desc: Copy of the jbeam nodes that have a couplerTag or a tag, keyed by node cid (fields couplerTag, couplerWeld, couplerLock, couplerStrength, couplerRadius, couplerLockRadius, couplerLatchSpeed, couplerTargets, couplerStartRadius, breakGroup, importElectrics, importInputs).

attachedCouplers.desc: Couplers currently attached, by local node cid: {obj2id, obj2nodeId, exportElectrics?, exportInputs?}.

update.desc: nop except during the progressive precompression of beams/torsion bars; called by the physics loop.

updateRemoteElectrics.desc: nop by default; becomes the real function after sendExportCouplerData. Called twice by electrics.lua: merges into electrics.values the values received from a coupled vehicle. Parameter retainReceivedElectrics: if false/nil, empties the received list.

debugDraw.desc: nop by default; draws spheres on the free coupler nodes whose tag is visible (setCouplerVisiblityExternal).

setPartCondition.desc: Would apply an integrity/visual state to a part. In this version the body is almost empty (the useful code is commented out): does nothing useful.

getPartCondition.desc: Estimates the state of a part from its broken breakGroups and deformed beams (`beamDamage`). The part (which must have a flexbody) is said to need replacement if too many groups are broken (>1, or all), more than 1% of beams are deformed (>= 0.01) or more than 2 beams are broken (>= 0.9).

returns.desc: {integrityValue, integrityState, visualValue, visualState}; visualState.needsReplacement = true and integrityValue = 0 if the part is too damaged.
true if a state could be provided.

breakBreakGroup.desc: Breaks a group: marks it in brokenBreakGroups, hides the group's props, breaks all its beams, detaches its couplers and breaks the collision triangles of the same group. Also notifies the camera if it is an occupant group (ocpAttach...).

g.desc: Name of the breakGroup. nil: does nothing.

setCouplerVisiblityExternal.desc: Called by another vehicle (via BeamEngine:queueAllObjectLua) to enable/disable the highlighting of couplers whose tag is in the list. (The name contains the typo "Visiblity".)

visibleTags.desc: Visible tags; false/nil disables the display.

activateAutoCoupling.desc: Enables automatic coupling: for 60 s max, every 0.5 s the couplers (all, or those of the given tags) are rearmed via attachCouplers. Broadcasts tag visibility to other vehicles. Without argument, also arms the `couplings` extension. Does nothing if the vehicle has no tagged coupler.

_nodetag.desc: Coupler tag(s) to target; nil = all free couplers (neither welded nor locked).

disableAutoCoupling.desc: Stops automatic coupling, clears the visible tags and notifies the couplings extension.

attachCouplers.desc: Arms (obj:attachCoupler) the non-welded couplers carrying a couplerTag, with their jbeam parameters (couplerStrength default 1000000, couplerRadius 0.2, couplerLockRadius 0.025, couplerLatchSpeed 0.3, couplerTargets 0).

_nodetag.desc: Processes only this couplerTag; nil = all.

couplerExists.desc: Indicates whether a coupler tag (couplerTag or tag) exists on this vehicle.

returns.desc: true if it exists, otherwise nil.

detachCouplers.desc: Detaches (obj:detachCoupler) the couplers of a tag or all of them. Locked or welded couplers are ignored unless forced. Notifies the game (onCouplerDetach) and the couplings extension.

toggleCouplers.desc: Toggles couplers; called when the L key is pressed. Without tag: stops auto coupling if active, detaches everything if a coupler is attached, otherwise starts auto coupling. With a tag: detaches if attached, otherwise attaches it (unless forceAutoCoupling).

forceAutoCoupling.desc: With a tag, forces the automatic coupling logic.

couplerFound.desc: C++ hook called when a nearby coupler is found. Empty body in this version (only a commented-out print).

obj2nodeId.desc: cid of the other vehicle's node.

sendExportCouplerData.desc: Asks the other vehicle (queueObjectLuaCommand -> exportCouplerData) to export certain electrics/inputs values to us, and activates updateRemoteElectrics.

obj2nodeId.desc: cid of the other vehicle's coupler node.

onCouplerAttached.desc: C++ hook called when a coupler attaches. Records the coupling in attachedCouplers, copies the lock/weld flags between couplers of the same vehicle, stops auto coupling if it was for this tag, requests the import of electrics/inputs if the node has importElectrics/importInputs, restores its coupler breakGroups, then notifies the game (onCouplerAttached on the GE side, only once: by the vehicle with the lowest id).

obj2nodeId.desc: cid of the other vehicle's node.

onCouplerDetached.desc: C++ hook called when a coupler detaches. Removes the coupling, breaks the node's breakGroups if breakGroupType is 0 or nil, then notifies the game (onCouplerDetached on the GE side, only once per pair).

obj2nodeId.desc: cid of the other vehicle's node.

breakForce.desc: Break force passed to the game.

getCouplerOffset.desc: Returns the position of each coupler relative to the vehicle's reference node (refNodes[0].ref).

couplerTag.desc: Filter on couplerTag or tag; nil or "" = all.

returns.desc: Per cid: {x, y, z, couplerTag, tag}. Empty table if there are no nodes.

exportCouplerData.desc: Called from the vehicle that wants to import electrics. On the provider, adds the requested electrics/inputs to the list sent every frame (in updateGFX) to the other vehicle.

nodeid.desc: cid of the local coupler node.

importCouplerData.desc: Called by the provider host. Stores the received electrics (then merged into electrics.values by updateRemoteElectrics) and replays the inputs via input.event(name, value, 2). Ignores the data if the coupler is no longer attached.

requestSkeletonState.desc: Sends the beam state (`beamDamageTracker`) to the UI via guihooks "VehicleSkeletonState" if a player is seated in this vehicle. Also called every 0.25 s when damage has changed.

deflateTire.desc: Deflates a tire. On the first call for the wheel: marks isTireDeflated, displays the message, plays the burst sound, records the damage, calls the hook `onTireDeflated(wheelid)` via extensions.hook, adds 1000 to damageExt and softens the beams of the tread, sidewalls and pressure. Subsequent calls increment the counter; beyond 4 the pressure group is emptied.

delPlanet.desc: Removes a planet (gravity attractor) identified by exact center, radius and mass, then updates the engine.

addPlanet.desc: Adds a planet (attractor) via obj:setPlanets. With dt, the planet is temporary: if it already exists with dt > 0 its duration is extended, with dt = 0 it is removed.

setPlanets.desc: Replaces all planets. The array is read in triplets (center, radius, mass).

updateGFX.desc: Called every graphics frame. Handles the timers of temporary planets, recomputes `damage`, the damage score per part, sends the skeleton state to the UI (at most every 0.25 s), drives automatic coupling (60 s timeout) and passes the requested electrics/inputs to coupled vehicles.

registerExternalCouplerBreakGroup.desc: Registers a coupler node cid in a breakGroup, so that a later breakBreakGroup detaches it. Used by coupling extensions.

torsionBarBroken.desc: C++ hook called when a torsion bar breaks. If it has a breakGroup, hides the props and breaks the group (breakGroupType 0 or nil), as beamBroken does for beams.

id.desc: Index of the torsion bar in v.data.torsionbars.

beamBroken.desc: C++ hook called when a beam breaks. Updates the damage tracking (body zone, part), deflates the relevant tire or pressure group, breaks collision triangles and meshes, rails, propagates to the breakGroup (breakGroupType 0/nil), changes the material (deformSwitches) and spawns particles (plastic, glass, wood).

isTriangleBroken.desc: Indicates whether a collision triangle is broken (absent from the internal tracking).

init.desc: Rebuilds the whole state from `v.data`: resets damage to zero, empties caches, reindexes triangles, breakGroups, deformGroups, couplers, beam tags, body zones, part data; prepares the delayed precompression, the part signal list, and registers the couplers radial menu. Called when the vehicle loads.

onBeamDeformed.desc: C++ hook called only for beams that have a deformation threshold. Updates `deformedBeams`, zone and part damage, changes material (deformSwitches) and counts the events of the deformGroup(s).

reset.desc: Reinitializes the state (calls init) and resets `lowpressure` to false. Called on vehicle reset.

breakAllBreakgroups.desc: Breaks all beams that have a breakGroup (obj:breakBeam) and also breaks the groups that contain only couplers.

breakHinges.desc: Breaks the beams with a breakGroup containing "hinge" or "latch" (hinges, latches), as well as coupler groups of this type.

deflateRandomTire.desc: Deflates a randomly chosen tire among those not already deflated.

triggerDeformGroup.desc: Triggers the material change of the first deformSwitches matching the given deform group.

group.desc: Name of the deformGroup; nil does nothing.

addDamage.desc: Adds artificial damage to `damageExt` (and therefore to `damage`).

requestSkeleton.desc: For the UI: sends the beam geometry (pairs of node positions) via guihooks "VehicleSkeleton", then the skeleton state. Does nothing displayable if no player is seated.

hasCouplers.desc: Indicates whether the vehicle has at least one non-welded coupler carrying a couplerTag.

couplerTag.desc: Filter on couplerTag or tag; nil = all.

save.desc: Writes a JSON ("v2" format) of the state: node positions and masses, rest length, beam breakage and deformation, hydro state and serialized Lua packets.

load.desc: Reloads a file written by save. Checks that the number of nodes/beams, the vehicle folder and the format match, otherwise logs an error and aborts. Restores nodes, masses, lengths, broken/deformed beams then calls obj:commitLoad().

getVehicleState.desc: Returns a snapshot of the vehicle (id, parts conditions, config itemId, position, front and up vectors). Contains a deliberate fake 1 s delay (see notes).

....desc: Values returned as is after the state.

returns.desc: The extra arguments passed as input.

getPartDamageData.desc: Returns the parts with strictly positive damage.

returns.desc: partPath -> {name, damage}; damage = max(broken beams / threshold, deformed beams / threshold), between 0 and 1.

getPartDamageScores.desc: Flat table signal-name -> damage score for all parts, including those at 0.

returns.desc: Short part name (or path with "_" in case of duplicates) -> score 0 to 1.

getPartDamageBySignalName.desc: Damage score of a part from its signal name.

returns.desc: Score 0 to 1, nil if the name is unknown.

getPartDamageSignalList.desc: Sorted list of available part signal names.

getBodyZoneDamageValue.desc: Damage of a body zone (sum of broken beams + deformation ratios, divided by the number of beams in the zone).

returns.desc: Damage value, 0 if the zone is unknown or empty.

getBodyZoneDamage.desc: Damage of the six body zones.

exportPartDamageData.desc: Writes the damage per part to the file `partDamage.json` (dumpToFile). Debug tool.

isPhysicsStepUsed.desc: Indicates whether beamstate needs the physics loop (true only while the delayed precompression is in progress).
